column3: A command-line tool for syncing project folders across machines
Tidewater 2.4 adds resumable transfers, a faster change scanner and a new configuration format. This document explains how to install the release and what changed since version 2.3.
1. Download the archive for your platform and unpack it into any folder.
2. Add the folder to your PATH.
3. Check the installation by running the command below.
The configuration file lives in the project root and is read every time the tool starts.

OptionTypeDefaultDescriptionsync.sourcepath.Folder to read changes fromsync.targetpathnoneDestination folder or network sharesync.excludelist[]Patterns that are never copiedretry.attemptsinteger3Number of tries before a transfer failsretry.delay_secondsinteger10Pause between two tries

Resumable transfers: an interrupted copy continues where it stopped. A change scanner that is about three times faster on large folders. A new configuration format based on YAML. Clearer error messages that name the file and the reason.
– The old .ini configuration file is no longer read.
– Exit code 4 now means a partial transfer and not an error.
CommandPurposetidewater syncCopy new and changed files to the targettidewater statusList files that differ from the targettidewater resumeContinue the last interrupted transfer
Use the preview flag to see what a sync would do without copying anything.
tidewater sync --preview\n3 files would be copied, 1 file would be removed
1. Paths longer than 260 characters are skipped on older Windows versions.
2. The status command may report a file twice if it is renamed during a scan.
Report problems on the project tracker and include the output of the status command.
